full_judgment:
Md Moinul Islam Chowdhury J: As the subject matters of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 33081 of 2014 and 33082 of 2014 are similar and the Rules were issued by this court on similar terms on the basis of similar legal and factual aspects, therefore, we are taking these two matters for disposal by this common judgment. 

 2. At the instance of the accused-petitioners, Mohammad Hossain and Mohammad  Rafiqul, these two Rules have been issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why accused-petitioners should not be enlarged on bail in the Metropolitan Special Case Nos. 139 of 2014 and 138 of 2014 arising out of Kalabagan Police Station Case Nos. 33 and 32 dated 31-7-2012, corresponding to ACC GR Case No. 123 of 2012 and 124 of 2012, under sections 4(2) of the Money Laundering Act, 2009 and section 4(2)(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 now pending in the court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka. 

 3. The relevant facts for disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33081 of 2014 are that the accused-petitioners No. 1 and 2 are the Chairman and the Managing Director respectively to a company known as Destiny 2000 Ltd., and the petitioner No. 2, is the Ex. President of Destiny Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd. 

 4. Md Toufiqul Islam, the Assistant Director of Anti-Corruption Commission lodged the First Information Report being Kalabagan PS case No. 32 dated 31-3-2015 under section 4(2)(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 alleging that Destiny Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd., (DMCSL) as a Co-operative Society having registered under the Co-operative Society Rule 2004 collected huge amount of money from ordinary persons by incorporating their names with Destiny Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd., Destiny Tree Plantation Ltd. and using the names of these companies the accused-petitioner No. 2 Mohammad Rafiqul Amin and others transferred and vested the money in different other companies. It is also alleged that the accused-petitioners along with others initially opened a company known as GGN and involved themselves in Multi-Level Marketing Policy (MLMP) type of activities thereby receiving ordinary investors by circulating that the said GGN Company was abolished and for the purpose of collecting money they thereafter incorporated the Destiny Multi-purpose Co-operative Society Ltd (DMCSL) and at one point of time as many as 8.5 lac members of DMCSL were collected who were made investor-share-holders. The petitioners started to receive commission of Taka 4,300 per package between the date of 11-10-2009 to 11-8-2010 in violation of the Co-operative Society Act, 2001 and also Cooperative Rules 2004, as such, the petitioners have committed offences by transferring and converting (অর্থ হস্তান্তর এবং রুপান্তর) received money illegally. In order to deceive the ordinary members and investors they marketed share in the name of DIBC package share and INDP package share, as such, in the fiscal year of 2009 and 2010 and upto 31-3-2012 they received money amounting to Taka 1935,53,20,000 and from the said amount the petitioners transferred money in the Destiny Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd Taka 7,333,129,643 as commission which is absolutely in contravention to the aforementioned co-operative laws thus the acts of the petitioners are punishable offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2012 (মানি লন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০১২) which came into operation on the 16th January, 2012 published in the Gazette Notification on 20-2-2012 and this FIR was lodged on 31-7-2012 for the dates of occurrence during the period of July, 2009 to May, 2012. 

 5. After making an investigation on the aforementioned allegations the investigating officer, Md Mozahar Ali Sarder, the Deputy Director, Durnity Daman Commission, Dhaka filed the charge-sheet No. 31 dated 30-3-2014 in the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka in the Special Case No. 139 of 2014 and this application filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for granting bail and the Rule was issued thereupon. 

 6. The relevant facts for disposal of the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33082 of 2009, inter alia, are that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 are the Chairman and the Managing Director of Destiny Tree Plantation Ltd registered with the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies and Firms incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994. 

 7. Mr Md Mozahar Ali Sarder, the Deputy Director of Durnity Daman Commission lodged the First Information Report being the Kalabagan PS Case No. 32 dated 31-7-2012 under section 13 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2002, section 4(2) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2009 and section 4(2)(3) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 alleging, inter alia, that in the name of Destiny Tree Plantation Ltd, (DTPL) started illegal business by selling trees during the period of 21-3-2006 to April, 2012 through advance sale and thereby collected huge amount of money from the ordinary people. Despite the facts the said company did not have permission to carry on Multi Level Marketing (MLM) as required under the company Act and thereby deceived the ordinary persons by selling the huge number of trees, even though, the trees were not in existence and from the said selling collected total Taka 23,357,485,500 and thereafter transferred and transformed the amount of Taka 21,066,465,500 to another company by the petitioners in the name of commission or premium by illegal means in contravention to the provisions of the aforementioned Act, 2002, Act, 2009 and the Act, 2012 (the Act 2002 and 2009 are now repealed). 

 8. After investigation into the aforesaid allegations the investigating officer in this case, namely, Md Towfiqul Islam, the Assistant Director, Durniti Daman Commission filed the charge-sheet No. 26 dated 20-3-2014 in the Court of Senior Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka in Metropolitan Special Case No. 138 of 2014 charging the present accused-petitioners and 17 others for commission of offences under the provisions mentioned above. The present accused-petitioners were allowed bail by the trial court but the bail was cancelled on a revisional application filed by the Commission on 11-10-2012 and thereafter the petitioners are in jail custody. This application has been made under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the accused-petitioners on bail and the Rule was issued thereupon. 

 9. Mr Ajmalul Hossain QC, the learned Senior Counsel appearing along with the other learned Advocates in both the Criminal Miscellaneous Cases in similar terms submits that the accused-petitioners have been in custody and the concerned authority permitted them to send on remand and both the accused-petitioners made confessional statements under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 25-10-2012 and 13-12-2012 respectively before the Magistrate as to the allegations and charges brought against them stating their involvement in the offences. 

 10. He further submits that according to the statements of the FIR no offence has been constituted under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2012 but the informant filed these cases preposterously against the accused petitioners and also submitted charge-sheets containing a huge number of pages with reproduction of same fabricated statements and, as such, the accused-petitioners may be enlarged on bail by this court. 

 11. The learned Advocate also submits that the actus reus for commission of offences as alleged took place during the period of July, 2006 to May 2010, as such, the petitioner cannot be held liable for any offences committed under the repealed law as there are no saving clauses under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012. He further submits that the allegations are that the petitioners have collected Huge amount of money by selling the trees on the basis of forward sale contract whereas there was no existence of the subject matter (trees) but the trees would have been in existence if the petitioners were allowed to mature their contracts in course of time thus these cases have been filed prematurely apprehending any future offences which is not sustainable under the provision of law and there was no illegal money received by deception thus there are no good reasonable ground for bringing the allegations thus the petitioner should be enlarged on bail. 

 12. The learned Advocate also submits that there are delay in lodging the FIR and also filing the charge-sheets after long period elapsed which is a good ground for bail and he further submits that in these two cases the vital questions are that what should be the prevailing operative laws at the trial of the cases because in the FIRs and the charge-sheets the petitioners have been charged under the provision of the Act, 2002, the Act, 2009 and the Act, 2012 relating to money laundering, as such, there are some errors in bringing these allegations, therefore, the petitioners should be granted on bail. 

 14. In the above Rules, both the applications filed under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure have been opposed by the opposite party No. 2, the Durnity Daman Commission contending that there are specific allegations against the petitioners in both the cases for transferring/transforming the money after collecting it illegally and by deceiving the ordinary people a huge money amounting to Taka 9,355,320,000 and 23,357,485,500 respectively. It is also contended that the petitioners have collected these amount by showing the Destiny Multipurpose Co-operative Society Ltd, and also by showing Destiny Tree Plantation Ltd, but most of the amount have been transferred or transformed in different companies in other illegal accounts in contravention to the provision of the Act, 2002, Act, 2009 and Act, 2012 regarding the money laundering provisions, as such, the petitioners are involved in the serious offences and the offences involving a huge amount of money which are serious and grave in nature therefore, bail should not be granted from this court. 

 15. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 2, the Durnity Daman Commission in both the cases submits that despite the facts of the offences committed by the accused-petitioners during the period of 2006 to 2012 they can be tried under the provision of Money Laundering Act, 2012 as the presently existing and prevailing law but the punishment, if any, should not be imposed more than the limit allowed under the prevailing law i.e. Act, 2002 or Act, 2009, as such, he submits that there is no illegality in bringing the charges under the Act, 2012 for the offence committed during the period of 2006 to 2009 and the said ground cannot be a valid ground for enlarging the accused-petitioners on bail. 

 17. The learned Advocate further submits that in the present case after filing charge-sheet, the cognizance has been taken on 11-6-2014 and the date has been fixed for framing charge on 27-5-2015 and he expects conclusion of the trial within short period of time thus at this stage this court should not grant bail. 

 18. Considering the above submissions made by the learned Advocates appearing for the respective parties and also considering the application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure along with the huge volume of Annexures therein, it appears to us that the accused-petitioners in both the cases are same and they are the Chairman and Managing Director of the Destiny Multipurpose and Co-operative Society Ltd as well as the Destiny Tree Plantation Ltd for which they obtained required approval from the Registrar of Co-operative Society and also from the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms within the provision of law. In course of their businesses the petitioners along with others of these two companies involved themselves in activities for selling shares upon planting trees which did not have any authorities in the maters of multi-purpose marketing as it was not within their permissible businesses. In the name of the same business the petitioners started collecting money by way of selling shares as well as receiving commission and premium from the ordinary people which were not permissible objects until 2009 but the acts of receiving commission were obtained illegally and unlawfully as these were beyond the provisions of their Articles and Memorandum of Associations as well as of the provision of the Companies Act, 1994. In such manner the petitioners and other co-accused have collected a huge amount of money. In the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33081 of 2011 the amount is total Taka 19,355,320,000 and in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33082 of 2011 the amount is total Taka, 23,357,485,500 and the same amount were transferred or transformed in the different companies such as Destiny 2000 Ltd and others, thereby the allegations have been brought in the FIRs and charge-sheets for commission of offences under the Money Laundering Act, 2002, the Act, 2009 and the Act, 2012. Now we need to examine the provisions of laws prevailing at different periods of time when the offences are alleged to have taken place. Firstly, section 2(ঠ) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 reads as follows: 

 22. The FIR have clearly mentioned about the involvement of the petitioners as being the supreme authorities of these Companies who are alleged to have involvement in these offences and the amount collected by the petitioners and other co-accused are huge which have been collected from the ordinary persons by allegedly practicing illegal means because they were selling the trees in the name of forward sale contract whereas there was no existence of those trees and the ordinary persons are still not aware whether those trees are in existence or not. In such situation, we consider that the allegation are serious and grave in nature and the trial of the cases in the presence of the petitioners are required when some of the co-accused are fugitive to law and some of the accused are absconding after obtaining bail from this court and some of the matters went up to the Appellate Division and directed the absconded accused persons to surrender but none of them has yet surrendered as per direction of the apex court. 

 23. Regarding the statements made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners as to the actus reus of the alleged offences are prior to the enactment of 2009, which is, under the repealed Act, 2002, therefore, the provision of law cannot be given a retrospective effect. In this regard Article 35 (1) of the Constitution of Bangladesh is only to prevent imposition of any punishment on the basis of the provision in the repealed Act but Article 35 of the Constitution has not prohibited from undertaking proceeding for trial of any case filed prior to the introduction of new laws. In support of this it can be referred to a case of Tarique Rahman vs Bangladesh reported in 63 DLR(AD) 2011, 18 wherein our apex court laid down the principle which reads as follows:- 

 "39. It is well established that legislature has full power to make a law with retrospective effect so as to destroy a right or a remedy altogether but this must be expressly laid down or by necessary implication in the repealing legislation. In the case of Motiur Rahman Khan vs Government of Bangladesh 34 DLR (AD) 321 it has been held that parliament being the supreme legislative authority subject to the constitutional limitations under Article 65 has the plenary power to pass any law on any subject both prospectively and retrospectively. But the parliament cannot pass a law to create a new offence which is not in existence at the time of commission of the act charged as an offence nor can it increase penal liability with retrospective effect. In the instant case the offence of money laundering under the Ain 2002 was alleged to have been committed from 1-1-2003 to 31-5-2007 and the procedure in respect of lodging complaint, holding investigation, trial and other related matters shall be initiated or continued under the ACC Act of 2004 and the ACC Rules, 2007. By incorporating the Ain of 2002 in the schedule to the ACC Act of 2004 the offence of money laundering was brought within the purview of the ACC Act of 2004 and no new offence was created nor any penalty was increased retrospectively rather the offence of money laundering under the Ain of 2002 was made tribal under the ACC Act of 2004 and the ACC Rules, 2007. It has not in any way created a new offence or increased penal liability retrospectively. Article 35(1) of the Constitution envisages the prohibition on conviction or sentence under an "ex post facto law" not trial of the offence alleged to have been committed or the procedure to be followed in the investigation, inquiry in respect of an offence alleged to have been committed." 

 24. As per the principles laid down by our apex court, such, we consider that there is no bar in continuing with the trial of the instant case under the provision of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012 but the punishment cannot be more than available under the prevailing law at the moment of time. 

 25. Regarding the submission made by the learned advocate for the petitioners on the similar footing with that other co-accused, namely, Lt. General Harunur Rashid who was granted bail. After examining the relevant documents we found that he did not make any confessional statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure but the present petitioners made confessional statements, as such, the submission of similar footing is not applicable in the present case. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 2 informed us that against the order for granting bail in favour of the said Harunur Rashid a petition has already been filed in the Appellate Division by way of Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal which is pending for disposal, therefore, submission of similar footing in the present case has no application. 

 26. On the basis of the above discussions as to the facts and the laws that a matter of bail is to be considered by a court where there is no prima facie case for believing that the involvement of the petitioners was not possible to be proved by the prosecution on the basis of the given facts or allegations brought in the FIR and the charge-sheet and also other materials after being adduced or produced by the prosecution in the trial but in absence of those required materials in a case a court should not grant bail on its own discretion. However, when the allegations and charges are serious and grave in nature or even where there are allegations for illegally obtained money and transforming thereof by the accused from a huge number of ordinary people and receiving a huge amount of money unlawfully from the ordinary people of the country in total nearly 4 crore which makes a court concerned about the morality of an accused person a court should not exercise the right under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the instant case, we have examined the documents carefully before us including lack of reasonable grounds for enlarging the petitioners on bail on the basis of the seriousness of allegations brought against the petitioners we are not inclined to enlarge the accused-petitioners on bail. 

 27. Accordingly we do not find any merit in the above Miscellaneous Cases being Nos. Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 33081 of 2014 and 33082 of 2014. 

 The learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka is hereby directed to take necessary steps for disposal of the Special Case Nos. 138 of 2014 and 139 of 2014 pending before him expeditiously.
